newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends weak as March/May spread unravels.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends weak as March/May spread unravels.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mostly lower amid steady pressure on the March/May spread, traders said.
"People are continuing to bash the front end," a KCBT trader said after the close.
The March/May spread traded as narrow as 30-1/2 cents per bushel before closing at 31-3/4 cents. It closed at just under 34 cents Thursday.
Traders said the weakness in KCBT wheat futures came after HRW wheat cash basis values weakened Thursday at interior and Gulf locations, signaling slack demand.
KCBT cash basis values were unchanged Friday.

KCBT March wheat also lost relative to CBOT March wheat, which was buoyed amid optimism for a large sale of U.S. wheat this weekend to Pakistan and prospects for further sales of wheat to Asian customers.
KCBT wheat closed two to four cents lower, with March down four cents at $4.15-3/4 a bushel.
Traders said Cargill Investors Services was a scale-down buyer of the March throughout the session. CIS bought 2.6 million March and bull-spread at least 700,000 March/May bushels.
